evidence.summary: 通过 Android 原生客户端连接 DeepSeek Harness，跟进会话、回答问题、审批命令并接收任务通知。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary:
核查 README.md、app/src/main/java/com/labteto/dshmobile/connection/ConnectionManager.kt、app/src/main/java/com/labteto/dshmobile/connection/HarnessClientFactory.kt、app/src/main/java/com/labteto/dshmobile/connection/HarnessSessionStore.kt、app/src/main/java/com/labteto/dshmobile/connection/RelayCredentialStore.kt、app/src/main/java/com/labteto/dshmobile/data/SessionStore.kt、app/src/main/java/com/labteto/dshmobile/notify/NotificationObserver.kt、core/src/main/kotlin/com/labteto/dshmobile/core/wire/ConnectionLoop.kt、core/src/main/kotlin/com/labteto/dshmobile/core/wire/DshApiClient.kt、core/src/main/kotlin/com/labteto/dshmobile/core/wire/HarnessSession.kt、core/src/main/kotlin/com/labteto/dshmobile/core/wire/RelayTls.kt、docs/SECURITY.md、docs/VALIDATION-0.16.0.md；直连先在根路径以启动token换取dsh-auth- cookie，交换不跟重定向，从Set-Cookie取name=value；relay走单独bearer和证书pin。HarnessClientFactory统一创建unary和mux，两者使用同一HTTP信任设置与对应credential，避免只给RPC认证而WebSocket漏凭据。其cookieFor条件是非relay，不只loopback，包含LAN直连。这里能证明客户端发何种认证，不能单独证明远端服务真正拒绝未认证者。

ConnectionLoop以remote.mux打开并收到$events ready为connected，记录clientId，断线关闭这一代mux并指数退避；3秒mux与5秒ready为不同失败预算。必须收到ready，任意其他首帧都不是连接成功。ConnectionManager对relay的trust fence、pin变化、未认证停止自动重试并保留错误，让用户重新配对或修复relay。

SessionStore审批先核本地待办与当前generation，构造ALLOWED_ONCE或REJECTED，再以clientId、eventId回答。DshApiClient按args封装$events/result，不自动重发失败答案；SessionStore区分宿主ok:false拒绝和载体失败，只有确实结束请求才清相应卡片，避免新问题被旧回答清走。旧代回答能否被宿主拒绝仍是协议依赖，客户端代码不能替宿主证明exactly-once。Transport失败命名Unsent也不能解释为远端未收到／未执行；应重连查询当前待办，不盲目重新批准。断开App或socket只是客户端退出，不是远端任务取消；停止任务需要单独宿主控制和结果确认。
limitations: 固定根Android客户端source研究，定向核Kotlin认证、mux ready／重连、审批结果与凭据／通知，辅以作者验证原件。未完整审所有UI、终端、插件管理、附件／Termux脚本、relay服务器或Harness服务端；未运行目标。Kotlin由固定git blob补读，不将JS/TS统计当全仓规模。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text: 已有受控Harness与Android手机的开发者离开桌面后处理等待、审批和结果。原办法是移动Web或返回电脑；合格结果是正确会话上的及时响应与可确认接管，执行能力仍由宿主提供。

固定根Android客户端source研究，定向核Kotlin认证、mux ready／重连、审批结果与凭据／通知，辅以作者验证原件。未完整审所有UI、终端、插件管理、附件／Termux脚本、relay服务器或Harness服务端；未运行目标。Kotlin由固定git blob补读，不将JS/TS统计当全仓规模。
独立非官方Android App，配合远端或Termux Harness；relay插件另仓。版本兼容与签名升级需核实际工件，不能因根列入目录就视为DSH插件。

#### 启动与依赖

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Android8+与可信APK | 必需 | 客户端界面与通知 | 不能由源码打包推断签名升级成功 |
| 可达兼容Harness与模型 | 必需 | 实际Agent执行 | 手机不是离线推理替代 |
| 启动token／cookie | 非relay直连需要 | RPC与mux认证 | 401需重新登录，非Host错误 |
| 独立relay与配对pin/token | 公网relay路径需要 | 身份与加密 | 外仓未审；QR与TOFU信任不同 |
| Termux及命令权限 | 本机运行可选 | 启停手机Harness | 权限是Termux用户执行范围 |

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 首次 | Android、宿主、可选relay／网络 | APK来源、版本、认证、通知配置 | 金额／工时未知 |
| 持续 | 模型推理、服务端、网络与电池 | 跟进结果、升级兼容与误批核对 | 未测比移动Web总收益 |
| 失败恢复 | 重连与重新配对 | 区分401/403/pin，核未知回答 | Unsent不证明未执行 |
| 退出 | 凭据和会话留存 | 本地清除加服务端撤销、收回暴露 | 客户端退出不终止远端任务 |
[Q03](#research-q03) 先以USB／可信测试网和非敏感任务确认后台通知、待办重放与错误提示，保留桌面核对。公网前另审relay，丢回答响应先核当前待办；无法及时或明确确认便撤销凭据回原Web。

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
|---|---|---|
| 离桌提醒 | 按设置和事件发原生通知 | 手机后台及时性和节时 |
| 审批正确定位 | generation/clientId/eventId及条件清卡 | 服务端旧代拒绝与丢响应真实行为 |
| 连接信任 | direct cookie与relay pin/token分路 | 服务端权限实现和跨版本兼容 |
| 作者验证 | 有固定alpha.2测试记录及跳过项 | 不等本轮当前设备／签名升级通过 |
[Q02](#research-q02) core协议与Android连接层分离，统一factory和ready代次、失败不重发、条件清卡处理真实远端时序问题。[Q03](#research-q03)文档认证描述漂移和直连cookie存储注释的loopback假设值得纠正，不能仅依据README宣称安全。
[Q01](#research-q01) 与 [Q02](#research-q02) 支持原生通知与远程待办接管的组合增量，特别是把认证、mux代次与回答eventId统一，避免把旧卡片和新请求混在一起。创新归于移动工作流与协议适配，不把Harness执行或relay服务器能力算本根原创。
[Q03](#research-q03) 安全文档与真实cookie路径存在冲突，直连cookie也不同于relay token的Keystore保护；手机登录仍获得工具能力，TLS不能缩小权限。[Q02](#research-q02) 载体失败虽称Unsent，却不证明远端未收到，用户仍须重连核待办，不能盲目再次批准。
[Q04](#research-q04) 从载体失败语义推导“宿主接受结果未知”的可见提示和待办核对入口，可能减少重复批准；尚未实现或试验。对照丢响应、旧generation和双端并发反例，重复操作不降或恢复投入增即否定。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) novelty25%是成熟Android通知与Remote协议适配超无增量0%；无新基础机制不足50%。[Q02](#research-q02) mechanism50%以generation/eventId和条件清卡解决远端回答时序，超界面移植25%；依赖宿主拒旧代且未验丢响应不足75%。transferability25%Kotlin core分离Android超全耦合0%，但依赖具体Harness协议不足50%。[Q03](#research-q03) simplification50%统一RPC/mux凭据超散落组装25%；多种信任路径与relay配置不足75%。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) workflow50%通知把离桌等待引回任务，超仅浏览入口25%；真实及时性未测不足75%。delivery25%增加移动待办可见性超0%，任务安全验收仍宿主不足50%。[Q03](#research-q03) reach50%明确Android离桌人群可进入全功能控制超局部便利25%；需Harness/网络和高权限不足75%。economics0%：相对移动Web未识别已实现的成本结构或资源组织创新；原生通知与移动便利已计workflow/reach，潜在节时不构成25%经济机制增量，总投入尚未测。

recommendation.reason: 已有受控 Harness 的 Android 开发者可先通过 USB 或可信测试网络，用 DSH Mobile 跟进非敏感任务并验证过期审批与重连。相比手机浏览器，它集中原生通知和按连接代次处理的待办回答，但手机登录仍具有工具执行权限。若通知不及时、回答状态无法确认或兼容排障超过收益，就撤销相关凭据并回到原 Web 与桌面操作。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) README28-34的离桌续办、NotificationObserver143-198的需动作通知连到明确等待步骤，重复摩擦与需及时接管后果超过50%用途明确，取75%；未有持续需求直接用户证据不足100%。

advantage.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 原生通知与[Q02](#research-q02) SessionStore2018-2040的待办映射超Web入口包装25%，取50%；通知及时性/误批收益和文档冲突不足75%。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) token交换、统一factory、ready/clientId、审批和错误清卡接线完整，且[Q03](#research-q03)核失败范围，支持源码50%超局部25%；作者alpha.2实验不是本轮当前手机验收，不足75%。

cost.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03) README连接路径和凭据store明确首次、持续、恢复与撤销退路，超过25%难以退出；取50%因仍需网络/服务端/版本和后台通知维护，未证明75%负担轻。

# DSH Mobile > 通过 Android 原生客户端连接 DeepSeek Harness，跟进会话、回答问题、审批命令并接收任务通知。 ## 研究范围 - **仓库**：[sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile) - **版本号**：未声明（[固定提交 93a79102f78a7afdb567aee7189cc7965955a1ba](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/tree/93a79102f78a7afdb567aee7189cc7965955a1ba)） - **版本日期**：2026-10-22（固定提交日期，北京时间；不是包发布日期） ## 结论状态 固定Kotlin支持移动通知、凭据与generation回答机制；真实手机后台行为、当前服务端兼容和用户效果未由本轮验证。未知结果提示仅未来假设。 ## 洞察短评 - **用途**：已有受控Harness与Android手机的开发者离开桌面后处理等待、审批和结果。原办法是移动Web或返回电脑；合格结果是正确会话上的及时响应与可确认接管，执行能力仍由宿主提供。 - **亮点**：[Q01](#research-q01) 与 [Q02](#research-q02) 支持原生通知与远程待办接管的组合增量，特别是把认证、mux代次与回答eventId统一，避免把旧卡片和新请求混在一起。创新归于移动工作流与协议适配，不把Harness执行或relay服务器能力算本根原创。 - **思考**：[Q03](#research-q03) 安全文档与真实cookie路径存在冲突，直连cookie也不同于relay token的Keystore保护；手机登录仍获得工具能力，TLS不能缩小权限。[Q02](#research-q02) 载体失败虽称Unsent，却不证明远端未收到，用户仍须重连核待办，不能盲目再次批准。 - **建议**：[Q04](#research-q04) 从载体失败语义推导“宿主接受结果未知”的可见提示和待办核对入口，可能减少重复批准；尚未实现或试验。对照丢响应、旧generation和双端并发反例，重复操作不降或恢复投入增即否定。 采用建议：[Q03](#research-q03) 先以USB／可信测试网和非敏感任务确认后台通知、待办重放与错误提示，保留桌面核对。公网前另审relay，丢回答响应先核当前待办；无法及时或明确确认便撤销凭据回原Web。 ## 核心贡献 [Q01](#research-q01) 与 [Q02](#research-q02) 支持原生通知与远程待办接管的组合增量，特别是把认证、mux代次与回答eventId统一，避免把旧卡片和新请求混在一起。创新归于移动工作流与协议适配，不把Harness执行或relay服务器能力算本根原创。 ## 关键质疑 [Q03](#research-q03) 安全文档与真实cookie路径存在冲突，直连cookie也不同于relay token的Keystore保护；手机登录仍获得工具能力，TLS不能缩小权限。[Q02](#research-q02) 载体失败虽称Unsent，却不证明远端未收到，用户仍须重连核待办，不能盲目再次批准。 ## Replies stream in with their reasoning, code blocks and tool calls. You\n can attach photos and files, reference files with `@`, and run commands and skills with `/`.\n- Press and hold a message, a tool call or a file to see what else you can do with it. The host writes the bytes\n * verbatim and answers with a receipt that a later `session/prompt` or `commands/execute`\n * cites by [FileUploadValue.receiptId]; the bytes themselves never ride a prompt.\n *\n * A carrier 404 means no route claimed the path — a deployment that composes no file-upload\n * service, or a relay that does not proxy it — and surfaces as `capability-unavailable` so a\n * caller can fall back to [fileUploadEncoded].\n */\n suspend fun uploadFileBinary(\n sessionId: String,\n name: String?,\n contentLength: Long,\n body: InputStream,\n onProgress: ((sent: Long) -> Unit)? = null,\n ): RpcResult {\n val query = \"sessionId=${encodeQueryComponent(sessionId)}\" +\n if (name != null) \"&name=${encodeQueryComponent(name)}\" else \"\"\n return try {\n val response = transport.upload(\n \"$FILE_UPLOAD_PATH?$query\",\n \"application/octet-stream\",\n contentLength,\n body,\n onProgress,\n )\n when (val result = decodeFromJsonElement(RpcResultJsonSerializer, WireJson.parseToJsonElement(response.body))) {\n is RpcResult.Ok -> try {\n RpcResult.Ok(decodeFromJsonElement(FileUploadValue.serializer(), result.value))\n } catch (e: CancellationException) {\n throw e\n } catch (e: Exception) {\n RpcResult.Err(notAHarness(\"upload value decode failed: ${e.message}\"))\n }\n is RpcResult.Err -> result\n }\n } catch (e: RpcTransportException) {\n RpcResult.Err(transportError(e))\n } catch (e: SerializationException) {\n RpcResult.Err(notAHarness(\"upload result decode failed: ${e.message}\"))\n } catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) {\n RpcResult.Err(notAHarness(e.message ?: \"invalid upload result\"))\n }\n }\n\n /**\n * `pluginInventory/list` — the host's composed-plugin inventory (read-only).\n *\n * Rows are decoded individually, as in [commandsList]: a future `fiberPhase` this build has\n * never heard of should cost that one row, not the whole list. A deployment that does not\n * compose the inventory plugin answers 404, which surfaces as `capability-unavailable` and is\n * the caller's cue to hide the section rather than report a failure.\n */\n suspend fun pluginInventoryList(): RpcResult =\n when (val result = callEmpty(\"pluginInventory/list\")) {\n is RpcResult.Ok -> {\n val entries = (result.value as? JsonObject)?.get(\"entries\") as? JsonArray\n RpcResult.Ok(\n PluginInventorySnapshot(\n entries = entries.orEmpty().mapNotNull { row ->\n runCatching {\n decodeFromJsonElement(PluginInventoryEntry.serializer(), row)\n }.getOrNull()\n },\n ),\n )\n }\n is RpcResult.Err -> result\n }\n\n /** `fileReferences/list` — file-reference completion candidates for a composer mention. */\n suspend fun fileReferencesList(sessionId: String, query: String): RpcResult =\n call(\n \"fileReferences/list\",\n args {\n put(\"agentId\", JsonPrimitive(sessionId))\n put(\"query\", JsonPrimitive(query))\n },\n )\n\n // ------------------------------------------------------------------ remote events\n\n /**\n * Answer one pending Remote Event waterfall.\n *\n * This is what replaced `POST /api/respond`. The reply is bound to a generation by\n * [clientId] — from the current `$events` ready frame — and to one pending request by\n * [eventId]; the host refuses a reply carrying a retired generation, so an answer typed\n * before a reconnect cannot resolve a request the host has since replayed.\n *\n * A failure here is deliberately not retried: upstream fails the whole connection generation\n * on it and replays the pending event on the next one, so a client-side retry queue would\n * answer the same request twice.\n *\n * It goes through [call] like every other unary, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy:\n * the gateway reads `$events/result` as a Remote with one named parameter, so the three\n * fields ride inside `args` and a bare `{clientId, eventId, outcome}` payload is refused\n * outright — \"Remote event result requires exactly one plain-object args field\". Through\n * 0.11.2 this posted that bare object, so every answer and every approval failed on the\n * wire while the app reported it as a connection fault.\n */\n suspend fun answerEvent(\n clientId: String,\n eventId: String,\n outcome: RemoteEventOutcome,\n ): RpcResult = call(\n REMOTE_EVENT_RESULT_ENDPOINT,\n encodeToJsonElement(\n RemoteEventResult.serializer(),\n RemoteEventResult(clientId = clientId, eventId = eventId, outcome = outcome),\n ).jsonObject,\n JsonElement.serializer(),\n )\n\n // ------------------------------------------------------------------ downloads\n\n /**\n * `session.export` — streams the session-log ZIP.\n *\n * The harness's one non-envelope read channel, and the one route that kept its 0.1.1 shape:\n * a plain `GET` answered with an attachment, registered as an exact fetch route rather than\n * as a Remote, because a browser download manager consumes a streamed response rather than a\n * JSON result. [consume] receives the live stream and must not retain it.\n */\n suspend fun sessionExport(\n sessionId: String,\n includeDescendants: Boolean = false,\n consume: (contentType: String?, contentDisposition: String?, body: InputStream) -> T,\n ): RpcResult = try {\n val query = \"sessionId=${encodeQueryComponent(sessionId)}\" +\n if (includeDescendants) \"&includeDescendants=true\" else \"\"\n RpcResult.Ok(transport.download(\"/api/session.export?$query\", consume))\n } catch (e: RpcTransportException) {\n RpcResult.Err(transportError(e))\n } catch (e: IOException) {\n RpcResult.Err(RpcError(\"internal\", e.message ?: \"download failed\", JsonObject(emptyMap())))\n }\n}\n" }, { "path": "core/src/main/kotlin/com/labteto/dshmobile/core/wire/HarnessSession.kt", "content": "package com.labteto.dshmobile.core.wire\n\nimport java.io.IOException\nimport java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit\nimport kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers\nimport kotlinx.coroutines.withContext\nimport okhttp3.OkHttpClient\nimport okhttp3.Request\n\n/** What a launch-token exchange produced, or why it did not. */\nsealed class SessionExchange {\n /** The `Cookie` header value to send on every later request to this authority. */\n data class Granted(val cookie: String) : SessionExchange()\n\n /**\n * The harness answered but issued no session.\n *\n * Almost always a token from an earlier harness process: the token rotates on every start and\n * is never persisted, so a startup URL copied yesterday is simply not the current one.\n */\n data class Refused(val status: Int) : SessionExchange()\n\n /** The exchange never reached a harness. */\n data class Unreachable(val kind: TransportFailure, val message: String?) : SessionExchange()\n}\n\n/**\n * The browser-session exchange harness 0.1.2 requires before any `/api` call.\n *\n * From 0.1.2 the harness authenticates its complete API — every Remote call, the mux upgrade, and\n * the session-log download — against a signed cookie, and answers 401 without one. The only way\n * to obtain that cookie is to present the launch token the harness prints once per process to its\n * *index* route: `GET /?token=…`. The token is deliberately refused on `/api` paths and in an\n * `Authorization` header, so there is no alternative to this exchange and no way to fold it into\n * an ordinary call.\n *\n * This is for **direct** connections. Behind `dsh-relay` the relay holds the harness session and\n * injects it upstream, and a phone that sent the host's cookie across the network would be\n * carrying a credential it has no business holding.\n *\n * Nothing here retries. A refusal means the token is not current, and asking again with the same\n * one produces the same answer.\n */\nobject HarnessSession {\n\n /** Cookie names the harness issues; the suffix is the normalized authority it is bound to. */\n private const val COOKIE_PREFIX = \"dsh-auth-\"\n\n /**\n * Exchange [token] at [baseUrl] for a browser session.\n *\n * Redirects are not followed: a successful exchange answers 3xx to the clean `/`, and the\n * cookie is on *that* response. Letting the HTTP layer chase it would discard the header this\n * whole call exists to read.\n */\n suspend fun exchange(\n baseUrl: String,\n token: String,\n client: OkHttpClient,\n timeoutMs: Long = 10_000,\n ): SessionExchange = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {\n val exchanger = client.newBuilder()\n .followRedirects(false)\n .followSslRedirects(false)\n .connectTimeout(timeoutMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)\n .readTimeout(timeoutMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)\n .build()\n val url = resolveHarnessUrl(baseUrl, \"/\").newBuilder().addQueryParameter(\"token\", token).build()\n val request = Request.Builder().url(url).get().build()\n try {\n exchanger.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->\n val cookie = response.headers(\"Set-Cookie\")\n .firstOrNull { it.startsWith(COOKIE_PREFIX) }\n // Only the name=value pair travels back; `Path`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite`\n // are instructions to a browser, and repeating them on a request would be\n // sending the server its own directives.\n ?.substringBefore(';')\n if (cookie != null) SessionExchange.Granted(cookie) else SessionExchange.Refused(response.code)\n }\n } catch (e: IOException) {\n SessionExchange.Unreachable(TransportFailures.classify(e), e.message)\n }\n }\n\n /**\n * Pull a launch token out of whatever the user pasted.\n *\n * People copy the whole startup line, the whole URL, or just the token. Accepting all three\n * costs one function and removes the one step where a working token gets rejected for having\n * a `?token=` in front of it.\n */\n fun tokenFrom(input: String): String? {\n val trimmed = input.trim()\n if (trimmed.isEmpty()) return null\n val marker = trimmed.indexOf(\"token=\")\n val candidate = if (marker >= 0) {\n trimmed.substring(marker + \"token=\".length).takeWhile { it != '&' && !it.isWhitespace() }\n } else {\n trimmed.takeWhile { !it.isWhitespace() }\n }\n return candidate.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }\n }\n}\n" }, { "path": "core/src/main/kotlin/com/labteto/dshmobile/core/wire/RelayTls.kt", "content": "package com.labteto.dshmobile.core.wire\n\nimport java.security.MessageDigest\nimport java.security.cert.CertificateException\nimport java.security.cert.X509Certificate\nimport java.util.Base64\nimport javax.net.ssl.HostnameVerifier\nimport javax.net.ssl.SSLContext\nimport javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager\nimport okhttp3.OkHttpClient\n\n/**\n * Transport trust for a `dsh-relay` listener, pinned to its public key.\n *\n * The relay's default posture is a self-signed certificate whose SHA-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo it\n * publishes in the pairing QR. Pinning the *key* rather than the certificate is deliberate on the\n * relay's side — it can renew with the same key without breaking paired devices — and it is what\n * this file compares.\n *\n * OkHttp's own `CertificatePinner` cannot do this job alone. Pinning runs *after* the trust manager\n * has accepted the chain, so a self-signed certificate is rejected by the platform CA store before\n * the pin is ever consulted. The pin has to *be* the trust decision, which is what\n * [pinnedClient] installs.\n *\n * Pure JVM (`javax.net.ssl`), so `:core` stays free of Android imports.\n */\nobject RelayTls {\n\n /**\n * SHA-256 of a certificate's DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64.\n *\n * `PublicKey.getEncoded()` on an X.509 certificate is the DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, so this is\n * byte-for-byte the value the relay publishes (`spkiFingerprint` in the plugin's `src/tls.ts`,\n * which exports the key as `spki`/`der` and base64s its SHA-256).\n */\n fun spkiPin(certificate: X509Certificate): String =\n Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(\n MessageDigest.getInstance(\"SHA-256\").digest(certificate.publicKey.encoded),\n )\n\n /**\n * A client that records the key it is offered and trusts it.\n *\n * This is trust on first use, and it is not a substitute for [pinnedClient]. It exists because\n * two of the relay's own flows cannot pin in advance:\n *\n * - **Passcode pairing.** The user reads a code off the relay's screen and types the address\n * themselves; there is no QR, so there is no fingerprint until the claim answers with one.\n * - **Liveness probing.** Asking an address whether it is a relay happens before this device has\n * any relationship with it at all.\n *\n * Neither sends a credential, and the claim that follows is a single-use code that is worthless\n * once consumed — but an attacker who can answer on that address during pairing does end up\n * holding the enrolment. That is a real difference from the QR flow and the UI has to say so\n * rather than let \"paired\" mean two different things.\n *\n * [observed] receives the presented key, so the caller can store the pin it actually spoke to.\n */\n fun trustOnFirstUseClient(base: OkHttpClient, observed: ObservedKey): OkHttpClient {\n val trustManager = LearningTrustManager(observed)\n val context = SSLContext.getInstance(\"TLS\")\n context.init(null, arrayOf(trustManager), null)\n return base.newBuilder()\n .sslSocketFactory(context.socketFactory, trustManager)\n .hostnameVerifier(HostnameVerifier { _, _ -> true })\n .build()\n }\n\n /**\n * A client that trusts exactly one public key.\n *\n * The hostname verifier passes unconditionally, and that is not a hole: the trust manager has\n * already refused every certificate but the pinned one, so the key *is* the identity and the\n * SAN adds nothing. It matters in practice because the relay's generated certificate covers the\n * addresses it saw at generation time, and a phone may reach it by an address — a port-forwarded\n * name, a VPN address — that was never in that list.\n *\n * There is deliberately no fallback to CA validation when the pin misses. A relay whose key\n * changed is an event the user has to see, not one to paper over: it means either a\n * regenerated certificate (the plugin mints a new key whenever its address set changes) or\n * somebody else answering on that address.\n */\n fun pinnedClient(base: OkHttpClient, fingerprint: String): OkHttpClient {\n val trustManager = PinnedTrustManager(fingerprint)\n val context = SSLContext.getInstance(\"TLS\")\n context.init(null, arrayOf(trustManager), null)\n return base.newBuilder()\n .sslSocketFactory(context.socketFactory, trustManager)\n .hostnameVerifier(HostnameVerifier { _, _ -> true })\n .build()\n }\n}\n\n/**\n * The served certificate did not carry the pinned public key.\n *\n * A distinct type rather than a bare [CertificateException] so the failure survives the wrapping\n * OkHttp does — it reaches the app as an `SSLHandshakeException` with this as a cause — and can be\n * reported as \"this relay's certificate changed\" instead of a generic TLS error.\n */\nclass PinMismatchException(\n val expected: String,\n val presented: String,\n) : CertificateException(\"relay public key does not match the pin recorded when this device paired\")\n\n/** Trusts one public key and nothing else. See [RelayTls.pinnedClient] for why this replaces the CA store. */\nprivate class PinnedTrustManager(private val fingerprint: String) : X509TrustManager {\n\n override fun checkServerTrusted(chain: Array?, authType: String?) {\n val leaf = chain?.firstOrNull()\n ?: throw CertificateException(\"relay presented no certificate\")\n val presented = RelayTls.spkiPin(leaf)\n // Constant-time is pointless here — the expected value is public, printed on the relay's own\n // pairing page — but a plain equality on two base64 strings is also the whole check, so it\n // is written out rather than hidden behind a helper.\n if (presented != fingerprint) throw PinMismatchException(fingerprint, presented)\n }\n\n /** This client never presents a certificate; the relay never asks for one. */\n override fun checkClientTrusted(chain: Array?, authType: String?) {\n throw CertificateException(\"dsh-relay clients do not present certificates\")\n }\n\n /** Empty on purpose: no issuer is acceptable, only the pinned leaf. */\n override fun getAcceptedIssuers(): Array = emptyArray()\n}\n\n/** Somewhere for [RelayTls.trustOnFirstUseClient] to report the key it was offered. */\nclass ObservedKey {\n @Volatile\n var pin: String? = null\n internal set\n}\n\n/** Accepts any server key and records it. See [RelayTls.trustOnFirstUseClient] for what that costs. */\nprivate class LearningTrustManager(private val observed: ObservedKey) : X509TrustManager {\n\n override fun checkServerTrusted(chain: Array?, authType: String?) {\n val leaf = chain?.firstOrNull()\n ?: throw CertificateException(\"relay presented no certificate\")\n observed.pin = RelayTls.spkiPin(leaf)\n }\n\n override fun checkClientTrusted(chain: Array?, authType: String?) {\n throw CertificateException(\"dsh-relay clients do not present certificates\")\n }\n\n override fun getAcceptedIssuers(): Array = emptyArray()\n}\n" }, { "path": "docs/SECURITY.md", "content": "# Security\n\nDSH Mobile is a remote control for the **DeepSeek Harness**. Understand the\ntrust model before using it — and note that the app offers three, which is why\nthe connect screen makes you pick one rather than choosing for you.\n\n## The thing to understand first\n\nThe harness is a coding agent. It runs shell commands, reads and writes files,\nand can install software on the computer it runs on. **Anything that can reach\nit can do all of that.** There is no lesser tier of access. All three modes\nbelow grant the same power; they differ only in what has to be true before\nsomeone gets it.\n\n## This phone (Termux) mode\n\nThe harness runs on the phone itself, inside Termux, and the app reaches it at\n`127.0.0.1`. Nothing leaves the device: the harness keeps its loopback bind,\nloopback clears its trust fence without configuration, and the sign-in cookie\nthe app holds is the same one it would hold for `adb reverse` (see **What DSH\nMobile stores**). Whoever holds the phone unlocked holds the agent — which is\nalready true of the Termux session next to it.\n\nTwo things are new in this mode, both opt-in:\n\n- **The app can run commands in Termux.** Start, Stop and Install via Termux go\n through Termux's `RunCommandService`, behind a permission Termux itself\n declares (*Run commands in Termux environment*). Granting it lets DSH Mobile\n run anything the Termux user can; the app asks for it only when Start, Stop or\n Install is tapped, never on launch, and runs nothing while it is in the\n background. What it runs is fixed and documented in\n [`harness/TERMUX.md`](../harness/TERMUX.md): a start script (wake lock,\n `dsh web --no-open --port …`, wait for the readiness line, print it back), a\n stop script that signals only the process it recorded, and a download script\n for updates. The scripts ship inside the app; nothing is installed in Termux,\n and the only values spliced into them are the port and the release URLs, both\n validated and quoted. Termux additionally requires `allow-external-apps = true`\n in its own `termux.properties` before it accepts any of this. Revoke the\n permission in Android's app settings to withdraw it all.\n- **The launch token is read from the harness's own output.** Since harness\n 0.1.2 a direct client must present the launch token the harness prints once per\n process. When the app starts the harness, it reads that line from the process\n it launched and exchanges the token at once — the same exchange it performs\n when you paste the line, with the same cookie stored in the same place. The\n token never leaves the phone and is never stored.\n\nA harness you start yourself in Termux is treated exactly as any other direct\nharness: found by probing loopback, signed in by pasting its startup line once.\n\n## Local network mode\n\nThe harness web server (`dsh web`) serves plain HTTP with a *trust fence*, not\nauthentication:\n\n- Every `/api` request is accepted only when its `Host` header is loopback or a\n configured trusted authority (LAN IP literals are auto-derived when the server\n binds `0.0.0.0`).\n- There are no tokens, cookies, or TLS. Any device on the same network can send\n requests with a trusted `Host` and drive the agent — including running\n commands on the host computer. TLS can be added from outside by fronting the\n harness with a reverse proxy — see **HTTPS through a reverse proxy** below —\n but that encrypts the link without authenticating anyone; only a relay does\n both.\n\n**Consequences:**\n\n- Only bind the harness to `0.0.0.0` on networks you fully trust (home network,\n your own lab). Never on public or guest Wi-Fi.\n- DSH Mobile states this on the connect screen whenever local-network mode is\n selected.\n- Sensitive surfaces (settings, credentials, agent-preset authoring, host file\n pickers) are **no longer loopback-only**. Harness 0.1.2 deleted that method\n tier and replaced it with one uniform rule: whoever holds a browser session\n reaches the complete tool-capable API. Behind a relay, what gates those\n surfaces is the relay's own `privilegedMethods` policy — set it to\n `loopback-only` if a paired phone should not reach them.\n\n## Relay mode\n\n[`dsh-relay`](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay) is a harness\nplugin that mounts a second listener beside the harness rather than inside it.\nThe harness keeps its loopback bind; the relay terminates TLS, authenticates,\nand forwards. A relay that fails to start therefore leaves the harness\n**unreachable** from the network — never open to it.\n\nWhat that gets you, and what it does not:\n\n- **A real credential.** The app holds a bearer token issued once, at pairing,\n and sends it on every `/api` call and both WebSocket upgrades. The relay stores\n only a keyed hash of it.\n- **Real transport security.** Traffic is encrypted, and the app pins the\n relay's public key by SHA-256 of its DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo. Pinning\n *replaces* CA validation rather than following it, so a self-signed relay is\n verified rather than merely accepted.\n- **Revocation you control.** Each device is individually revocable from the\n relay's own device list, and \"sign out everywhere\" invalidates every token at\n once. Either one surfaces in the app as \"pair again\" on the next request.\n- **It does not reduce what an authenticated client can do.** Signing in grants\n the same power as a shell on that machine. The question the relay answers is\n \"is the remote user you\", not \"how much can the remote user do\".\n\n### How the key is established\n\nTwo pairing routes, and they do not prove the same thing. The app says which one\nhappened rather than reporting \"paired\" twice:\n\n- **Scanning the QR** carries the relay's key in the payload, so the very first\n byte the app sends is verified against it.\n- **Typing the code** carries no key — the relay only reveals one in its answer\n to the claim — so the certificate is trusted on first contact. An attacker able\n to answer at that address during pairing would end up holding the enrolment.\n\nPrefer the QR. The typed route exists because it is the one that works when the\ncamera does not.\n\n### When the key changes\n\nThe relay regenerates its certificate — with a **new key** — whenever the set of\naddresses it covers changes. A harness laptop that moves between networks\ntherefore rotates its pin, and paired devices stop connecting until they pair\nagain. That is indistinguishable from something else answering at the address,\nso the app reports it as a changed key and refuses to proceed on its own.\n\n### What is not defended\n\n- **A weak relay password.** Ten characters is the enforced floor, not a\n recommendation.\n- **A relay running `tls: off`, or its plain-HTTP compatibility listener.** The\n token and everything you send travel in the clear. The app says so on the\n pairing screen and on the endpoint's card.\n- **Source-address grants.** The relay's `compat.addressGrants` accepts requests\n from an address a paired device was last seen on, as a bridge for clients that\n cannot hold a token. A source address is not authentication: it is shared\n behind NAT, reassigned by DHCP, rotated by IPv6 privacy extensions, and\n spoofable on the same Wi-Fi. **This app no longer needs it** — set\n `compat.addressGrants: false` once every client you use has paired.\n\n## HTTPS through a reverse proxy\n\nThe harness itself never serves TLS, but the app can reach one behind a\nreverse proxy that does (Caddy at `https://agent.home`, say). Typing\n`https://…` into the connect screen — or a bare address with port 443 —\nmakes the whole connection TLS: every `/api` call, both event streams, and\nsession-log downloads.\n\nCertificate verification is standard Android, with one addition:\n\n- The app trusts the system CA set **plus CAs the user has installed** on the\n phone (``). A LAN proxy is almost always signed\n by a local CA — Caddy's internal CA, mkcert, a homelab CA — which only\n works if the phone's owner has deliberately installed that CA, an act\n Android itself warns about and marks. The app adds no CAs of its own.\n- Verification is never relaxed beyond that. There is no \"accept this\n certificate anyway\" flow, no hostname-check bypass, and no pinning UI: an\n untrusted certificate fails the connection with a message naming the CA\n install as the fix.\n- Relay mode is the exception, and it goes the other way. There the app pins a\n key it was handed at pairing and ignores the CA set entirely — stricter than\n this path, not looser, and never something the user is asked to approve.\n- The trust fence still applies through a proxy. The app sends the authority\n it was given as the `Host` header, so the harness must be started with\n `--trusted-host ` (a proxy that preserves `Host`, as Caddy does\n by default, changes nothing about this).\n\n## File attachments\n\nSince harness 0.1.3 the app can attach any file to a message. The bytes are\nstreamed to the harness the moment the file is picked — over whichever\nconnection is in use, with the same credential and the same encryption, or\nlack of it, as everything else — and the harness writes them **verbatim** into\nits attachment store on the computer it runs on, where the agent's file tools\ncan read them. A file you attach is therefore a file you have copied onto that\ncomputer, into a directory the agent reads. In local-network mode that copy\ntravels in the clear.\n\nThe app keeps no copy: it reads the picked document once, at upload time, and\nholds only the receipt the harness answered with until the message is sent.\n\n## What DSH Mobile stores\n\n- Remembered endpoints (host, port, whether to use HTTPS, display name, and —\n for a relay — its device id and certificate pin) plus app preferences, in\n app-private storage only.\n- **Relay bearer tokens, encrypted.** The key is generated in the Android\n Keystore and never leaves it; only ciphertext reaches DataStore. Forgetting a\n host drops its token in the same act, and Settings → clear data drops all of\n them. Revoking the relay's own record of the device happens on the relay.\n- No session content is persisted to disk (chat history lives in memory and is\n re-fetched on connect).\n- Cleartext HTTP remains permitted app-wide, alongside user-installed CAs\n (`app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml`). Cleartext cannot be\n narrowed: a bare harness serves plain HTTP on a LAN address not known at build\n time. The app answers this by naming the transport wherever an endpoint\n appears rather than by pretending every connection is encrypted. A pinned\n relay bypasses that trust store entirely — the pin *is* the trust decision.\n\n## What DSH Mobile connects to\n\nEvery connection is to an endpoint you entered, scanned, or picked from a scan,\nwith one exception:\n\n- **The update check.** On start the app asks `api.github.com` for this\n repository's latest release, over HTTPS, so it can tell you when a newer APK\n exists. It sends no identifying information beyond what any HTTPS request\n carries, and it is the only request the app itself makes that leaves your\n network. Turn it off in **Settings → About → Check for updates**.\n- **Install via Termux**, when you tap it. Termux — not the app — downloads the\n release APK and `SHA256SUMS.txt` from `github.com` with `curl`, verifies the\n file, and opens Android's package installer, which asks you before anything\n is installed. Nothing is downloaded unless you tap the button.\n- **Scanning** probes only your own device's IPv4 /24 — with a TCP connect\n followed by one argument-free `session/canOpenWorkspacePath` call in\n local-network mode, or by `/relay/health` in relay mode. Relay mode browses mDNS `_dsh._tcp` first and only sweeps if that\n finds nothing.\n\n## Reporting a vulnerability\n\nReport security issues privately, either through **Report a vulnerability** on\nthe repository's Security tab or by email to **sor@zyphite.com**. Do not open a\npublic issue for a vulnerability.
